name: Saint-Simonianism
summary: Saint-Simonianism is the early French industrialist doctrine of Henri de Saint-Simon and his school, which held that society should be reorganised around productive work and led by scientists, industrialists and other capable people instead of idle nobles and clergy. It sought the fastest possible improvement of the poorest class, a planned and credit-directed economy, abolition of inheritance, and a reformed religion of brotherhood. After 1830 the school became a church-like movement under Enfantin that also demanded women's emancipation, and many members then turned to railways, banking and canal projects.
scope: Henri de Saint-Simon's late works, especially The New Christianity (1825), and the Saint-Simonian school of 1825-1832 (Bazard, Enfantin, Rodrigues), plus the movement's industrial and banking legacy (the Pereires, Crédit Mobilier, Suez). It excludes Comte's positivism as a separate doctrine and later technocracy generally. Many modern questions are anachronistic and answered by inference.

keyFigures.name: Henri de Saint-Simon

keyFigures.name: Prosper Enfantin
keyFigures.role: Leader of the school after 1830, 'Father' of the movement and advocate of the priest-woman

keyFigures.name: Amand Bazard
keyFigures.role: Co-leader and main lecturer of the Exposition, who split from Enfantin

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the goal of raising the poorest class as fast as possible, which favours organised public provision over charity.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage floors were not a school concern; it wanted the poor raised through productive organisation and pay by capacity, so no clear stance follows.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The school wanted industry planned by a hierarchy of experts and a state that centralises as industry concentrates, though Saint-Simon also admired Smith and distrusted heavy state interference.

public-ownership.rationale: Later Saint-Simonians wanted a state-guided industrial association with central banks and large works directed by leaders, with property returning to the association.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Abolishing inheritance and idle rentier income implies heavy burdens on unearned wealth, though taxation itself was not their device.

unions-good.rationale: Saint-Simonians wanted workers and industrialists as one productive class under common leadership, so independent labour unions were not their instrument.

property-fundamental.rationale: The school held that inheritance of property was a feudal survival to be abolished and that property should return to the association.

regulate-corporations.rationale: They wanted industry coordinated by an expert hierarchy rather than regulated from outside, so regulation is not the natural frame.

cut-welfare.rationale: The central precept is the fastest possible improvement of the poorest class's condition.

worker-ownership.rationale: Ownership was to pass to the whole industrial association run by a ranked hierarchy, not to each firm's workers.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Never addressed; an authority-friendly hierarchy and a liberal-industrial bent point in opposite directions.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; no principled position follows.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; the brotherhood ethic would disapprove of hatred but legal speech limits were not discussed.

strong-leader.rationale: Saint-Simon wanted an authoritative hierarchy of competent leaders chosen by co-option, which favours decisive guidance, though by experts rather than a single bypassing figure.

state-harmful.rationale: The school wanted an administrative-industrial order in which the state, as organ of centralisation, grows in role as industry concentrates.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; no inference possible from the doctrine.

empower-police-military.rationale: Saint-Simon wanted military and governing power replaced by industrial administration and criticised rule by physical force.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The Enfantin wing preached rehabilitation of the flesh but sex work as such was not a doctrine position.

decide-locally.rationale: Centralised direction by a unified hierarchy is a defining feature, not local autonomy.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the brotherhood ethic and its aim of improving the lot of the poor; penal policy was not discussed.

traditional-family.rationale: The Enfantin wing attacked traditional marriage, urged emancipation of women and a priest-woman, and the movement was tried for indecency.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; sexual-morals radicalism of the Enfantin wing gives no firm stance.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by the sources I read.

more-religion-public.rationale: The New Christianity wanted religion reformed to the social aim and the movement became a church with its own priesthood and rites.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Saint-Simon is described asserting Black inferiority and a technocratic internationalism that took racial hierarchy for granted, though the school's own stance is mixed.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The school demanded women's enfranchisement and emancipation, which implies social rather than natural limits, but the Enfantin wing also stressed sexual complementarity.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Saint-Simon proposed uniting Europe and treated industrial society as a European-wide project over national traditions.

gradual-change.rationale: They sought a rapid reorganisation of society by an elite leading change and rejected established feudal and clerical institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Nothing said; their cosmopolitan industrial and European vision leans against restriction.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Saint-Simon's 1814 essay proposed European institutions of common government.

free-trade.rationale: Saint-Simon admired Adam Smith and the followers (e.g. Chevalier) promoted exchange and communications between nations, with benefit to all.

nation-first.rationale: The doctrine put European and universal association ahead of narrow national interest.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not discussed; they favoured European organisation and colonising the world but not rights-driven intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Universal association was an aspiration but free movement was not discussed.

limit-growth.rationale: The whole program is expansion of industrial production to benefit the many.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; their productivist ethic and planning bent point opposite ways.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Saint-Simon believed science and industry could reorganise society and uplift all.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from enthusiasm for large-scale industrial and scientific energy projects.

revolution-justified.rationale: Saint-Simon wanted persuasion of elites and peaceful reorganisation; Marx faulted him for not seeking overthrow.

experts-over-public.rationale: Saint-Simon wanted scientists and industrial leaders to govern, with heads chosen by co-option and people only electing among them.

central-planning.rationale: The school wanted the economy planned and directed by an administrative hierarchy and is often counted among founders of planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: The question of markets under common ownership did not arise; they wanted planning rather than markets.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; they stressed abolishing inheritance rather than a land tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The school held that inheritance is a feudal survival to be abolished outright, which goes beyond taxing it.

basic-income.rationale: Pay by capacity and work for all, with an idle class condemned, cuts against unconditional income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Saint-Simon admired Smith and the school stressed open exchange, though state-led industry was favoured.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The school wanted banks and a central direction to channel capital to productive enterprises, later realised by Crédit Mobilier.

widespread-small-property.rationale: They wanted inheritance abolished and property pooled under one hierarchy, not spread widely among small owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Reward was to be by capacity and work; money and wages as such were not abolished.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: They favoured a central banking hierarchy directing credit, the reverse of abolishing it.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Industry led by a unified hierarchy resembles corporatism, but not state-recognised bargaining over wages and prices.

one-party-rule.rationale: They wanted a ranked elite and priesthood, not a party; parties as such were disliked as divisive.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Saint-Simon renounced his title and criticised hereditary rank, but his European kingdom idea and later Napoleon III collaboration show indifference to form.

democracy-best.rationale: Saint-Simon was explicitly not a democrat; leadership went by capacity and co-option with the people choosing from among them.

direct-votes.rationale: The school rejected popular rule in favour of an expert hierarchy.

workers-councils.rationale: Authority was to rest in committees of industrial leaders and scientists, not workers' bodies.

right-to-secede.rationale: Unity of Europe and the world in one system was the aim; secession not discussed.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rule by capacity was central, with a hierarchy of scientists, industrialists and priests ranked by talent.

political-violence-never.rationale: They addressed rulers who rely on physical force as wrong and sought reform by persuasion, though no absolute pacifism was proclaimed.

war-builds-character.rationale: They hoped for an end of military order in favour of industrial administration and peaceful association.

separate-church-state.rationale: They wanted a new religion integrated into social organisation, with spiritual and temporal authority united in a ranked hierarchy.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Dogma was secondary; Christianity was to be reduced to one principle of brotherhood, though morality was religiously grounded.

private-courts-defense.rationale: They wanted a centralised administrative order, not privatised justice and defense.

military-superiority.rationale: They sought replacement of military by industrial order, not rivalry for superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Saint-Simon's vision was European and universal, centred on association by function, not ethnicity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Saint-Simon read the Revolution as class conflict between industrial and idle classes but wanted harmony and rejected proletarian revolution.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Reward was to be by capacity and work, not equal shares, though the poor's welfare was prioritised.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Saint-Simon argued Europeans should colonise the world; indigenous rights were not discussed.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The movement's colonial and civilising bent gives no support for reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Saint-Simonians sought a union of East and West, but based on industrial association rather than shared religion alone.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The fundamental moral principle is that all must behave as brothers and work for the poorest class.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The social ethic stresses duty and ranked service to the community, and rights talk was not their frame.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Nature is the object of industrial development; intrinsic value was not discussed.

limit-population.rationale: Not discussed; their productivist outlook gives no clear stance.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The industrial transformation of society was the project's whole purpose.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Saint-Simon wanted science and industry to replace the old temporal and spiritual order and the school built railways and canals.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; faith in science supports it but no stance exists.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the idea of a scientific administration of things replacing political rule.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic and not related to their concerns.

restore-past-order.rationale: Saint-Simon wanted the feudal and theocratic order abandoned for an industrial future, and looked forward not back.

results-over-ideology.rationale: They insisted on a doctrine yet claimed scientific method; adherents were split.

direct-action.rationale: They worked through persuasion of rulers, bankers and industrialists rather than direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed; they hoped for peaceful brotherhood but through hierarchical means.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Industrial progress was the central aim.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Society was to be a ranked division of functions among scientists, industrialists and workers.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Reward by capacity and work was the formula, though the poorest were prioritised in welfare.

production-for-use.rationale: They wanted production serving the largest number and the poorest class, rather than the idle rich, though profit was not abolished.

profit-exploitation.rationale: They blamed inheritance and lending at interest for exploiting workers, not entrepreneurial profit; industrialists were productive leaders.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: They rejected class rule by workers and Marx faulted their hope in elite persuasion.

collective-farming.rationale: They proposed great public works to develop land, but not specific collective farming.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: They blamed idle military and feudal powers for war and expected industry to bring peace.

taxation-theft.rationale: The school wanted the state's role to grow with industry, not to be limited.

harm-principle.rationale: A morally directive priesthood and hierarchy would guide lives well beyond preventing harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Society as an organised association with functions took precedence over individual claims.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; they disliked military order but favoured disciplined organisation.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The freedom to leave was not their concern; they favoured organised collective direction.

state-as-business.rationale: Saint-Simon wanted administration by industrial managers but not customer-citizens.

positive-liberty.rationale: The material and moral improvement of the poorest class was the object of society, implying freedom needs material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: They wanted scientists to hold power, and the press (Le Globe) was their organ, but no claim about current power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Saint-Simon is reported to have asserted Black inequality with Europeans, but the school as a whole did not develop it.

organic-representation.rationale: Leadership by industrial and scientific functions rather than parties fits, though not families and communities.

total-state.rationale: A single organising hierarchy over economy, science and religion is close to total direction, but in the industrial rather than coercive form.

national-rebirth.rationale: They aimed at regenerating society but through industry and science, not national decadence narratives.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Saint-Simon urged European colonisation of the world, but the project was pacific and industrial.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The doctrine condemned feudal and force-based rule.

bound-labor.rationale: Feudal bonds were the old order they sought to replace.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: They believed objective science could ground society.

universal-morality.rationale: The New Christianity rests on the universal principle that all men are brothers, with moral science to be developed.

single-common-good.rationale: Society should aim at one end, the greatest benefit to the largest and poorest class, found by science.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed; some Jewish Saint-Simonians were prominent but no doctrine on this.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Nothing in the sources I read touches diasporas or return rights, and their universal association gives no pull either way.

revive-national-language.rationale: Universal association over national particularism, not discussed directly.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Industry was to be led by chosen competence, with ranks by co-option.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education was to be organised by the social hierarchy, not by parental market choice.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: They favoured credit creation and large investments by banks to fund great works.

economic-freedom.rationale: Saint-Simon wanted unhindered productive activity yet also planning and hierarchy; the school went further toward direction.

rule-by-example.rationale: The New Christianity urges rulers not to rest on force but on service; example is part, but they also wanted organised institutions.

national-self-determination.rationale: They envisaged European and universal association rather than nation-states as an end.

force-without-un.rationale: They favoured common European institutions and peaceful organisation.

reason-over-faith.rationale: They sought a scientific religion of brotherhood: reason matters but faith and a new religion were explicit.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The poor of all humanity as the object, so restricting to citizens clashes with their universal brotherhood.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The idle class was their main target and labour the source of social merit.

class-collaboration.rationale: Industrialists, scientists and workers are one productive class led by natural leaders, in contrast to the idle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The school valued art highly, drawing Berlioz and Liszt, though it urged forward-looking art.

dominated-front.rationale: They sought partnership between East and West and an industrial Europe.

workers-nation.rationale: Universal association rather than national classes.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The movement demanded women's enfranchisement, though Enfantin also saw complementary roles in the priest-couple.

ban-interest.rationale: The school held lending at interest is a feudal survival that enslaves the worker and should be abolished.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Brotherhood of all men conflicts with segregation, though Saint-Simon's own racial views were unequal.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state is the organ of social centralisation to be turned to production, not simply class domination.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from their pro-industrial output stance.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Their universal brotherhood and East-West union favour mixing over national cultural uniformity, but immigration policy was not discussed.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no basis in the doctrine.

proportional-representation.rationale: They favoured selection by capacity rather than party-list representation.

national-mission.rationale: Their mission was an industrial and religious one for all humanity, though France was seen as leading.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The school demanded women's emancipation, implying recognition of subordination, though the sources I read do not state a theory of patriarchy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Saint-Simon denounced idle nobility and rulers resting on force and wanted them displaced.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not discussed; they hostile to inherited privilege and would not coerce reproduction.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from their condemnation of rulers who rest on physical force; transitional justice itself was never discussed.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state was to be an expanding organiser of industry.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not discussed; Saint-Simonian East-West union and Enfantin's marriage of man and woman of different origins hint at opposite.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The precept of universal brotherhood supports equal worth, though in practice ranks by capacity and Saint-Simon's racial views were hierarchical.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from the single ranked order they proposed for all members of society, though religious personal law was never discussed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: They favoured a new universal faith by persuasion; conversion bans not discussed.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not discussed; industrial utilitarian outlook opposes.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: They wanted religion and education united in the new social order.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Authority rested on competence with the people only choosing among those qualified.

trade-surplus.rationale: They favoured open exchange rather than mercantilism.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: They criticised rule based on force but did not hold an absolute libertarian principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: They criticised anarchic competition and wanted organised cooperation, with industry in association.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Inferred: they saw parties as divisive and wanted administration by capacity, but banning parties was never discussed.

separated-powers.rationale: They wanted unified direction by a single hierarchy.

vanguard-party.rationale: A leading elite of scientists and industrialists resembles it, but for a harmonious order not revolution.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The New Christianity states the goal as the most rapid improvement of the condition of the poorest class.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Inferred: they wanted property to return to the association, not to be sold into households; housing was not discussed.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed; they wanted class harmony but not statute on strikes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: They blamed social organisation, idle classes and feudal survivals.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Their universal brotherhood and East-West union point the other way.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Ranks are by capacity with co-option, the opposite of lottery.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The sources say nothing on emergency powers, and an authoritarian streak points against a liberal brotherhood ethic.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from a planned economy directed by experts and the priority of the poorest; price fixing was never discussed.

party-controls-media.rationale: They ran their own paper Le Globe but did not call for state control of media.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not a party model; they sought a demilitarised industrial order.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Higher ranks were to be more rewarded by capacity.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The movement itself was a disciplined hierarchy and later a church, but parties were not their model.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Saint-Simon's 1814 essay proposed a European union with joint institutions.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Constitutional arrangements for command of the armed forces were never discussed in the sources I read.

church-by-bishops.rationale: They condemned existing hierarchies yet built a ranked priesthood with a pope-like Enfantin.

clerical-rule.rationale: Their own scheme combined spiritual and temporal leadership under a new priesthood, but of scientists and industrialists rather than religious scholars.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: They sought international peace by association rather than class defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: They treated art as a prominent role in work and an engine of social feeling.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred: leaders ranked by capacity and chosen by co-option would stay while competent, so term limits are not a principle.

recall-officials.rationale: Leaders chosen by co-option rather than recalled by voters.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Not addressed beyond European union ideas.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Property was to be held by the association and used by allocation, not universal ownership.

people-in-arms.rationale: They wanted military function replaced by industrial administration.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: They championed industrial and urban development of society.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Scientists and learned men were to lead society.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Saint-Simon assumed hierarchies of civilisation and European leadership.

death-penalty.rationale: Penal questions were not covered in the New Christianity or the reference accounts, and adherents had no set position.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the movement's women's emancipation and rehabilitation of the flesh.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: They advanced a scientific, positive outlook.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The Enfantin wing preached rehabilitation of the flesh, but nothing in the sources addresses legal limits on pornography.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language policy was not discussed; their universal association and nationalism-averse outlook give no push either way.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses exemptions from general law for religious minorities.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: They wanted a unified ordered society with a moral priesthood, not a Millian valuation of eccentricity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred: they were financiers and credit-builders who treated credit as an engine of development, so cancelling debts would sit badly with them.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Decolonial independence was not their frame; they favoured colonial development led by Europeans.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Authoritarian streak and prioritisation of industrial development imply tolerance of such limits.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Universal brotherhood and aid to the poorest class implies duty, though international aid was not their program.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Leaders were to be chosen by co-option up the hierarchy with the people only electing from qualified candidates.

central-bank-independence.rationale: They wanted a central banking system as an instrument of directed production, not insulated stable-price technocracy.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Their pacific, cosmopolitan outlook disfavours attachment to historic homelands.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: They held that property serves society's productive end and that inheritance should be abolished with property returning to the association.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anachronistic; not part of their frame.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from confidence in science and industry to progress.

collective-defense.rationale: Mutual defence pacts were not discussed; their aim was a peaceful European union replacing military order.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Annexation and occupation law was not discussed in the sources I read.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: They wanted a reformed church merged with a new social hierarchy, not curtailment under civil authority.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not discuss symbolic heads of state; Saint-Simon himself accepted a European king under England's lead.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses secession; their unifying bent leans toward holding together but no stance is documented.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses regional autonomy inside a larger state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Saint-Simon criticised rulers basing power on force and sought rule by competence and brotherhood, though Enfantin was treated as quasi-papal.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred; Saint-Simon wanted lower taxes yet prioritised the poor, not flat rates.

character-from-environment.rationale: Inferred from the belief that social organisation and moral science can transform the condition of the poor.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: They condemned rulers basing power on force; rule by capacity and administration was meant to serve society.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis beyond general optimism.

mixed-constitution.rationale: They wanted a single organised hierarchy of capacity, with the people choosing among qualified candidates.

leader-cult.rationale: The movement's veneration of Enfantin as father and of Saint-Simon as founder is akin, but the doctrine did not assert such a principle.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law was never discussed; the Enfantin wing's focus on the man-woman couple gives no rule here.

land-redistribution.rationale: They wanted property pooled in the association rather than land given to the farmers.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugees and return rights were not part of the doctrine as the sources describe it.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Contradicts their universalist European and world association.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: They sought a new faith by persuasion and condemned rulers who rely on force.

women-must-cover.rationale: They demanded emancipation of women and rehabilitation of the flesh.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from their European union and unified credit schemes.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: They proposed union by industrial and European association, not by ancestry.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The sources do not discuss national minorities or cultural autonomy.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed; some leading Jewish Saint-Simonians exemplify integration, but no doctrine.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Saint-Simon read the Revolution through economic change and class, but also gave science and religion central roles.

ban-cartels.rationale: Concentration of industry under unified direction was welcomed.

no-bailouts.rationale: State and banks were to direct credit to productive enterprise, not let them fail.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred: they wanted rule by capacity not majorities, yet courts were not discussed so confidence is low.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: They sought women's enfranchisement and joint rule by priest and priestess, but quotas were not discussed.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: They favoured European and global exchange, colonial and communications development.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anachronistic; their internationalism and concern for the poorest could support labour standards but nothing is documented.

moral-incentives.rationale: The New Christianity ties work to brotherly duty, but they kept reward by capacity.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: They worked by persuasion; Marx criticised exactly this reliance on elites.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The school demanded abolishing inheritance and Saint-Simon himself renounced his title and criticised hereditary rank.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Their view of European and universal history disfavours national centring.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Saint-Simon argued Europeans should colonise the world and accepted hierarchies of civilisation.

patriotic-education.rationale: They disfavoured nationalism for a European and universal association.

public-money-creation.rationale: They wanted a central bank hierarchy directing credit and issuing it for production, as in later Crédit Mobilier.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: They wanted to reform industry without overthrowing, and the Pereires built investment banking within it.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not addressed; their Mediterranean and Egypt projects show interest in influence but no doctrine on former empires.

delink-world-market.rationale: They favoured integration and global industrial exchange.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not discussed; they saw workers as one class with industrialists.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Contradicts brotherhood and organised social direction.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional bills of rights were not discussed; they favoured administrative hierarchy over legal limits on government.

elective-rulers.rationale: Capacity-based co-option rather than election was favoured.

minority-veto.rationale: A unified hierarchy directing society contradicts consent by every member.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: They criticised rulers relying on force but advised persuasion not resistance.

parliament-supreme.rationale: They wanted administration by the competent rather than a parliament as supreme.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animals do not feature in the New Christianity or in reference accounts of the doctrine.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use was never discussed; their productivist outlook would permit use but no position is documented.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: They urged the rich to fund productive works for the poor and not merely give charity.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: They were active organisers of industry and preached social engagement.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: They valued art as part of social work and mass communication as a tool.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Saint-Simon read class power through economic change, but the sources I read do not address cultural consent to rule.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: They held industry benefits all and favoured integration.

native-born-offices.rationale: Offices to capacity regardless of origin.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: They favoured large-scale joint investment and the movement of capital across borders.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Not an aim of a European industrial union.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: They favoured European leadership in colonisation.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic; fascism postdates the school by a century.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anachronistic; the question concerns twentieth-century regimes.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Anachronistic; the American Civil War came after the school dissolved.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Anachronistic; monument controversies play no role in the doctrine.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Anachronistic; the school's gender concern was women's emancipation, not male disadvantage.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Anachronistic; no discussion of domestic violence appears in the sources.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Their model was one universal industrial and religious order.

military-guardian-role.rationale: They wanted military authority replaced with industrial administration.

paid-care-work.rationale: Their women's emancipation did not extend, in the sources I read, to wages for care work.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed; Enfantin wing attacked traditional family forms.

office-by-exam.rationale: Posts by capacity and merit, hierarchy chosen by ability; this is akin to competitive selection even though co-option is the stated method.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the Enfantin wing's attack on conventional marriage and emancipation of women.

recallable-delegates.rationale: They rejected a delegate model of representation.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Welfare and savings were to be organised by the hierarchy.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Property to return to the association, but no use-based tenure was set out.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary budget control was not discussed; they preferred expert administration over parliaments.

single-official-language.rationale: Language policy was not addressed in the sources.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anachronistic; this is a modern legal doctrine with no analogue in the school.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: They disliked idle luxury but promoted abundance for all.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Peace and association, not covert war.

corporate-influence.rationale: Not addressed; industrialists were leaders by design.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population policy was never discussed in the sources I read.

residents-only-property.rationale: Property to be held by the association, not localistic.

job-guarantee.rationale: Society as an association of work, with the idle condemned, implies work for all, though no explicit guarantee is documented.

democratic-peace.rationale: Their path to peace ran via industry and association, not democracy.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: They wanted an obedient hierarchy of ranks.

non-intervention.rationale: They favoured European integration and colonisation.

industrial-unions.rationale: Labour organisation by craft or industry was not addressed; they wanted workers and industrialists in one productive class.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Contradicts the doctrine of universal brotherhood.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Enfantin wing attacked conventional marriage but the movement did not call for abolishing legal marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Information-access rights were not discussed, though they favoured a free press as the movement's organ Le Globe showed.

local-production.rationale: They favoured large-scale trade and communication works.

informal-organisation.rationale: They were a formally hierarchical movement.

religious-nation.rationale: Nation by function and universal faith, not national religion.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Central direction of resources was favoured.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Property was to be pooled but personal belongings were not discussed.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anachronistic; communism as a state project postdates the school.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Delivery of public services by mixed providers was not discussed; the school favoured a single directed system.

religion-illusion.rationale: The New Christianity argues for a religion of brotherhood as the basis of society.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Industry and its development were the progressive force, though they criticised idle owners and interest.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: They demanded women's emancipation and community of goods but sources do not link them.

socialized-care.rationale: Public provision of housework and childcare was not discussed in the sources, though women's emancipation was demanded.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations were not addressed; their colonising bent gives no sign they would honour such treaties.

cooperative-communities.rationale: They were a centralised hierarchy rather than small self-governing communities, even if the movement lived in communal households.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The school sought an organised industrial society beyond both idle capital and egalitarian revolution; Marx named them patriarchs of socialism.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic; contradicts the doctrine of brotherhood.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Enfantin's rehabilitation of the flesh implies opposition to such bans, but not directly stated.

suppress-opposition.rationale: They sought persuasion, though they admired hierarchy.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Dogma and ritual were secondary to them.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: They saw colonisation as bringing industrial improvement, not extraction.

participatory-democracy.rationale: They wanted an expert hierarchy with limited popular role.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Anachronistic; the school addressed class and women's status but not as intersecting.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; no discussion of gender identity appears.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Saint-Simon wanted to move beyond political parties to an administration of industry.

alienated-labor.rationale: They saw work as the basis of social value, not alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Contradicts universal brotherhood; the Saint-Simonians sought East-West union.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: They grounded morality in the Christian principle but authority in capacity.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious dress rules were not discussed; their new religion was meant to be integrated into society.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic; workplace harassment law has no analogue in the doctrine.

social-market-economy.rationale: A mix of social concern and market economy is close in spirit, but they favoured directed economy.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Saint-Simon wanted military order replaced by industrial administration.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred; industrialists lead first, with all to follow.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Military blocs were not an issue; their goal of European union led by one power does not settle neutrality.

dynastic-succession.rationale: They opposed hereditary privilege and called for abolition of inheritance.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: They opposed interest but wanted credit via a hierarchical banking system, not user-owned banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anachronistic; international lenders like the IMF did not exist, though the school valued credit.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not addressed; Enfantin wing stressed union of woman and man.

property-franchise.rationale: They wanted capacity not wealth to rank, and abolished inheritance.

reification.rationale: Marx's category is not part of the doctrine; Marx treated the school as precursors without sharing its framework.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The sources do not address ownership of the press; the movement ran its own paper Le Globe.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The sources do not address the rule of law as such; they preferred administrators directing production over governors commanding.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; the internet is unrelated to their expert-led structure.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic; open data is a modern concept with no analogue in the school.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The New Christianity reinterprets Christianity as one principle of brotherhood and condemns the clergy's heresy.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Not their frame; they welcomed concentration under industrial leadership.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Anachronistic; the question has no counterpart in a doctrine that wanted military order replaced.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: They wanted a new religion, not atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Their hierarchical, administrative order would keep public safety institutions, though policing was not discussed.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Divided societies were not the school's concern; their model was unitary expert direction.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The text says productive public works help the poor more than charity.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: delegated voting is a form of popular control, while they wanted rule by those with capacity.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic; extinction risk was not a concept of the period.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Enfantin wanted a priest-woman to share leadership and the school called for women's emancipation.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The school called for women's emancipation, and Enfantin treated the couple (man and woman) as the unit of religious authority.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not discussed; their cosmopolitanism and distrust of electoral rule balance out.

rent-control.rationale: Housing policy was not discussed; they favoured planned production over price caps.

abolish-ip.rationale: They favoured rewarding talent and industry.

uniformed-youth.rationale: They sought demilitarisation, though the movement wore uniforms.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; nuclear weapons postdate the school.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources do not discuss military basing.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The sources I read do not address recognition of past mass killings.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not addressed; their unit of concern was European and universal association.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Cross-border capital was central to their later ventures, such as the Pereires' European railways and banks.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Saint-Simon's central division is between a productive industrial class and an idling class living off others.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not addressed; the school's peace was about industrial association, not pacifism, so this is inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The doctrine looked to a universal industrial association rather than national origins; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The school demanded women's emancipation but did not discuss sex as constructed; inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Enfantin's school spoke of women as a category with a distinct mission; no clear position on this modern claim.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Its New Christianity stressed brotherhood and productive work, not national martyrdom; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Politics was to become the science of production, not a struggle of good and evil; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Anachronistic; the school's universalist association outlook gives no role to a diaspora homeland.

culture-before-state.rationale: The school sought to reorganise the state and economy around production first; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: After 1830 Enfantin's church sought a female messiah and a divine couple, suggesting support for non-exclusively male God language; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: The school's religion of brotherhood and demand for women's emancipation suggest judging tradition by its treatment of women; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The school's universal association rejected national or group reservation of economic life; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine was cosmopolitan and not concerned with ethnic territorial units.

independent-unions.rationale: Anachronistic; the school wanted industrial organisation led by capable administrators, and independent unions were not part of its doctrine.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Anachronistic; the school sought planned industrial society led by experts, which differs from the working-class power test, so this is a weak inference.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the aim of raising the poorest class and from public works and planned credit directed from above.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from the school's graded hierarchy of experts, which sits more naturally with a chamber of capable people alongside any elected body.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from its call for a centralised, credit-directed economy rather than local community ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from the school's centralised administration by experts, which is opposed to powerless coordination bodies.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed; the school rewarded each according to capacity and work, which cuts against family-based pay, but it also sought to lift the poorest.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its faith in science and industry as engines of progress.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its faith in science and the aim of improving the lot of the poorest class.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its credit-directed, centrally planned banking, which relies on oversight of money flows.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic and not discussed in the sources.

person-over-state.rationale: The New Christianity grounds society on brotherhood and the improvement of each person, especially the poorest, and condemns rulers who rule by force.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The New Christianity makes a reformed religion of brotherhood central, and the school became a church-like movement under Enfantin.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from the school's centralised, hierarchical administration, which leaves little room for regions with revocable powers; not directly stated.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the school's strong faith in science and industrial progress.

dense-cities.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the school's enthusiasm for railways, canals and industrial concentration of effort.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Anachronistic; the school's universal brotherhood and organisation by capacity rather than birth point firmly against race-based politics, though Saint-Simon held racial views.

racial-pride.rationale: Anachronistic; universal brotherhood runs against racial pride, though Saint-Simon's own racial views complicate this.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Not addressed directly; the school opposed rule by force and favoured peaceful European union, but also colonisation.

missingStatements.text: Property should not be passed down by inheritance but return to society to be reallocated by ability.
missingStatements.rationale: The school treated abolition of inheritance as a core demand, as a feudal survival that enslaves workers.

missingStatements.text: Society should be led by those whose useful productive work benefits the many, not by idle owners of inherited wealth.
missingStatements.rationale: Saint-Simon's central division is between a productive industrial class and an idling class living off others.

missingStatements.text: Each person should be ranked and rewarded according to their capacity and their work.
missingStatements.rationale: The school ordered society by capacity, with leaders drawn up the hierarchy on merit.

notes: The Saint-Simon of 1814-1825 and the Enfantin-led church of 1830-32 differ on several points (state size, sexual morals, religion). Answers follow the school's mainstream; most anachronistic questions are low confidence.
